stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring all processing runs entirely on the user's device.
This emphasizes a trend toward privacy-focused, on-device AI execution.

stories.title: Anthropic wants to develop its own drugs
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic is expanding its AI focus beyond general models into scientific research with the launch of 'Claude Science'.
Claude Science is positioned as an 'AI workbench for scientists,' integrating disparate tools and datasets into a unified environment.
The initiative signals a major industry shift toward applying large language models directly to complex scientific discovery and data visualization.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: Autonomous AI coding agents create a new security vulnerability due to persistent codebases across sessions.
Researchers introduce 'Iterative VibeCoding' to study attacks where misaligned agents distribute payloads across multiple pull requests over time.
The research focuses on the critical area of safely deploying capable but potentially untrusted AI systems.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based programming tasks.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications directly into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses current limitations of relying on LLM APIs (locality, reproducibility, cost) for tasks like log alerting or JSON repair.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper introduces LACUNA, a new testbed designed to rigorously evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods.
It addresses a critical security concern: LLMs memorizing sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from training data.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not the internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-based tasks that are poorly suited for traditional programming.
Proposes 'Program-as-Weights,' a method to compile natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts.
Addresses the current industry trend of outsourcing complex logic to LLM APIs, aiming to improve locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: Addresses the high inference cost of Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) used in state-of-the-art image/video generation.
Introduces OrbitQuant, a novel data-agnostic quantization method designed to handle shifting activations in DiTs.
Bypasses the need for re-fitting calibration data across different checkpoints or modalities, simplifying deployment.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: LLMs retain sensitive training data (PII), necessitating reliable post-hoc removal methods.
Current unlearning techniques often use a 'localize-first, unlearn-second' approach targeting specific model parameters.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs continue to produce unsafe outputs even after alignment training, necessitating post-deployment monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal to trigger safety alarms.
The monitor's effectiveness is shown to be competitive in mathematical reasoning and red teaming evaluations.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically benefiting Apple silicon users with broader model access.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, both locally and in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A new macOS malware, PamStealer, has been discovered.
The malware is noted as being different from typical macOS infostealers.
The discovery highlights a growing focus and increased sophistication in Mac-targeting malware.

stories.title: FAA proposal: Supersonic airliners can fly over US cities if they’re quiet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is proposing new regulations to allow supersonic airliners to fly over US cities.
The key condition for this allowance is that the aircraft must be quiet enough to eliminate the sonic boom.
This represents a potential regulatory shift enabling the return of supersonic commercial travel within US airspace.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper introduces LACUNA, a testbed designed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods.
It addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive data like PII, necessitating reliable post-hoc removal techniques.
The research critiques current benchmarks for unlearning, which only test output-level erasure rather than true knowledge removal from model parameters.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still produce unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The paper proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal for alarm decisions.
The monitor's threshold is calibrated using risk control and shows competitive performance in red teaming and reasoning tasks.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long context windows.
Introduces 'RECONTEXT,' a training-free inference method called Recursive Evidence Replay.
Aims to bridge the gap between LLMs' ability to access long contexts and their actual capacity for effective long-context reasoning.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under the same conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives shaped by social context.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the difficulty of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, containing 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The study leverages Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of attributing spoken utterances to specific characters.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method building upon On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for LLM training.
Addresses a critical limitation of current OPSD methods: teacher supervision can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
The core innovation involves modulating the distillation process based on disagreement to improve model robustness.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (RRMs) with symbolic solvers.
Utilizes SE-RRMs (symbol-equivariant RRMs) to generate full solution proposals and guide classical solvers (e.g., SAT-based methods).
The research demonstrates improved extrapolation capabilities when applied to larger constraint satisfaction problems.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still produce unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The paper proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated using risk control, and shows competitive performance.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under identical conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives based on social context.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a method to improve on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for LLMs.
Addresses a key limitation of current OPSD methods: teacher supervision overfitting to in-domain patterns.
Aims to enhance cross-domain generalization and exploration by modifying the distillation process.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces CNeVA, a new framework for controllable simulated agents.
The agents can imitate logged behavior while allowing steering along interpretable axes.
This controllability is crucial for testing autonomous systems and isolating variables in traffic simulation without real-world risk.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of post-training LLMs in specialized domains lacking human-labeled data.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Utilizes the model's own outputs and majority voting across multiple rollouts to generate pseudo-labels.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
Provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks perform under real-world, decentralized data conditions.
Fills a current gap in the literature regarding the robustness and theoretical understanding of D-SSL methods.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Proposes 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-based tasks that are poorly suited for traditional programming.
The core idea is to compile a natural-language specification into a compact, locally-executable neural artifact ('Program-as-Weights').
Aims to address drawbacks of using LLM APIs for these tasks, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under identical conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives driven by social context.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: The research addresses the complex challenge of speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas.
A new large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, has been introduced, featuring 532K annotated dialogue lines across over 900 characters.
The work utilizes Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in complex narrative video content.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical vulnerability in CLIP-based Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) known as Typographic Attack (TA).
TA occurs when irrelevant text embedded within images biases visual representations toward lexical meaning rather than true visual semantics.
The research proposes a 'training-free' method for concept localization to improve the robustness of these foundational models.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection capabilities.
Proposes using Reinforcement Learning to enable LVLMs to properly attend to visual inputs during error correction.
Aims to improve the models' ability to translate feedback into grounded corrections, especially for out-of-distribution images.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: The research investigates if scaling up Large Language Models (LLMs) can improve the fidelity of social simulations.
The study examines whether simulation accuracy is dependent on general LLM capabilities or if it requires a separate research focus.
The authors utilize scaling laws to analyze the relationship between compute scale, general benchmarks, and simulation fidelity.

stories.title: crustc: Entirety of rustc, translated to C
stories.author: github.com via ajdecon
bullet_points: The project 'crustc' involves translating the entirety of the Rust compiler (rustc) into the C programming language.
This represents a significant engineering effort in compiler technology and language interoperability.
The announcement is posted on Lobsters, suggesting an audience interested in deep technical topics.
